verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI ships its own AI assistant surfaces: the `clai` CLI for chatting with LLMs from the terminal or a browser, and an overview claim of 'a complete coding agent in your terminal' with file access, an allowlisted shell, and planning. That is first-party delegation to an assistant, but the product is mainly a framework for building agents, and the evidence on the built-in assistant is thin. missing for 10: detailed docs on what tasks the built-in coding agent can take on end-to-end, evidence the assistant is integrated inside the product rather than offered as a separate CLI, and independent hands-on corroboration of delegating tasks to it.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: A complete coding agent in your terminal: workspace-rooted file access, allowlisted shell, repo orientation, planning, and context management that survives long sessions.
You can use it to chat with various LLMs and quickly get answers, right from the command line, or spin up a uvicorn server to chat with your Pydantic AI agents from your browser.
Pydantic AI comes with a CLI, clai (pronounced “clay”).
